claim: Chromatin boundaries subdivide eukaryotic chromosomes into functionally autonomous domains of genetic activity.
source: Chromatin boundaries subdivide eukaryotic chromosomes into functionally autonomous domains of genetic activity.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that represents established scientific knowledge about chromatin boundaries.

claim: Chromatin boundaries insulate genes and/or regulatory elements within a domain from promiscuous interactions with nearby domains.
source: This subdivision insulates genes and/or regulatory elements within a domain from promiscuous interactions with nearby domains.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract describing the function of chromatin boundaries based on established knowledge.

claim: It was previously assumed that the chromosomal domain landscape is fixed.
source: While it was previously assumed that the chromosomal domain landscape is fixed, there is now growing evidence that the landscape may be subject to tissue and stage specific regulation.
evidence: This statement references prior assumptions in the field, supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: There is growing evidence that the chromosomal domain landscape may be subject to tissue and stage specific regulation.
source: While it was previously assumed that the chromosomal domain landscape is fixed, there is now growing evidence that the landscape may be subject to tissue and stage specific regulation.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations in the introduction discussing dynamic domain landscapes.

claim: Elba is a novel developmentally restricted boundary factor.
source: Here we report the isolation and characterization of a novel developmentally restricted boundary factor, Elba.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Elba is an unusual hetero-tripartite protein complex.
source: We show that Elba is an unusual hetero-tripartite protein complex that requires all three proteins for DNA binding and insulator activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by in vitro reconstitution experiments and mass spectrometry data.

claim: All three Elba proteins are required for DNA binding.
source: We show that Elba is an unusual hetero-tripartite protein complex that requires all three proteins for DNA binding and insulator activity.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro translation experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: All three Elba proteins are required for insulator activity.
source: We show that Elba is an unusual hetero-tripartite protein complex that requires all three proteins for DNA binding and insulator activity.
evidence: This is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 9.

claim: Boundary elements have an enhancer-blocking or insulator activity.
source: The specific functions that can be ascribed to most boundary elements include an enhancer-blocking or insulator activity (Holdridge and Dorsett, 1991; Kellum and Schedl, 1991; Chung et al., 1993), a silencer-blocking or barrier activity (Kellum and Schedl, 1991; Chung et al., 1993; Burgess–Beusse et al., 2002) and, when combined in specific pairwise combinations an ability to bring distant chromosomal DNA segments in close proximity (Cai and Shen, 2001; Muravyova et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Boundary elements have a silencer-blocking or barrier activity.
source: The specific functions that can be ascribed to most boundary elements include an enhancer-blocking or insulator activity (Holdridge and Dorsett, 1991; Kellum and Schedl, 1991; Chung et al., 1993), a silencer-blocking or barrier activity (Kellum and Schedl, 1991; Chung et al., 1993; Burgess–Beusse et al., 2002) and, when combined in specific pairwise combinations an ability to bring distant chromosomal DNA segments in close proximity (Cai and Shen, 2001; Muravyova et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Boundary elements can bring distant chromosomal DNA segments in close proximity when combined in specific pairwise combinations.
source: The specific functions that can be ascribed to most boundary elements include an enhancer-blocking or insulator activity (Holdridge and Dorsett, 1991; Kellum and Schedl, 1991; Chung et al., 1993), a silencer-blocking or barrier activity (Kellum and Schedl, 1991; Chung et al., 1993; Burgess–Beusse et al., 2002) and, when combined in specific pairwise combinations an ability to bring distant chromosomal DNA segments in close proximity (Cai and Shen, 2001; Muravyova et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Cai and Shen, 2001 and Muravyova et al., 2001.

claim: In S. pombe, boundaries help restrict and maintain the heterochromatin state of the silenced mating type locus.
source: In the yeast S. pombe, boundaries help restrict and maintain the heterochromatin state of the silenced mating type locus (Noma et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Noma et al., 2001.

claim: In Drosophila, boundary elements play a critical role in the Bithorax complex helping to ensure that the three BX-C homeotic genes properly specify segmental identity.
source: In Drosophila, boundary elements play a critical role in the Bithorax complex (BX-C), helping to ensure that the three BX-C homeotic genes properly specify segmental identity (Maeda and Karch, 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Maeda and Karch, 2006.

claim: In vertebrates, boundaries have been implicated in controlling the expression of mRNAs encoding different neuronal Protocadherin-alpha isoforms.
source: In vertebrates, boundaries have been implicated in controlling the expression of mRNAs encoding different neuronal Protocadherin-alpha isoforms and in regulating recombination and expression of immunoglobulin light and heavy chain genes (Guo et al., 2011; Ribeiro de Almeida et al., 2011; Monahan et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Guo et al., 2011; Ribeiro de Almeida et al., 2011; Monahan et al., 2012.

claim: In vertebrates, boundaries have been implicated in regulating recombination and expression of immunoglobulin light and heavy chain genes.
source: In vertebrates, boundaries have been implicated in controlling the expression of mRNAs encoding different neuronal Protocadherin-alpha isoforms and in regulating recombination and expression of immunoglobulin light and heavy chain genes (Guo et al., 2011; Ribeiro de Almeida et al., 2011; Monahan et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Guo et al., 2011; Ribeiro de Almeida et al., 2011; Monahan et al., 2012.

claim: The first boundaries identified were able to block adventitious regulatory interactions irrespective of cell type or developmental stage.
source: The first boundaries identified were able to block adventitious regulatory interactions irrespective of cell type or developmental stage (Gyurkovics et al., 1990; Holdridge and Dorsett, 1991; Kellum and Schedl, 1991; Chung et al., 1993).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to early boundary studies.

claim: Proteins conferring insulating activity in flies and vertebrates like Su(Hw), BEAF, Zw5, GAGA factor and CTCF are ubiquitously expressed.
source: Moreover, the proteins conferring insulating activity in flies and vertebrates like Su(Hw), BEAF, Zw5, GAGA factor and CTCF are ubiquitously expressed and seemingly functional in all cell types.
evidence: This statement represents established knowledge about known insulator proteins.

claim: The regulatory domain landscape of eukaryotic chromosomes is more dynamic than previously imagined.
source: However recent studies argue that the domain landscape is more dynamic than previously imagined and that genes can be differentially regulated during normal development and differentiation and in the progression of disease states like cancer by redefining their domain organization (Bell and Felsenfeld, 2000; Witcher and Emerson, 2009; Gomes and Espinosa, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Bell and Felsenfeld, 2000; Witcher and Emerson, 2009; Gomes and Espinosa, 2010.

claim: Genes can be differentially regulated during normal development and differentiation by redefining their domain organization.
source: However recent studies argue that the domain landscape is more dynamic than previously imagined and that genes can be differentially regulated during normal development and differentiation and in the progression of disease states like cancer by redefining their domain organization (Bell and Felsenfeld, 2000; Witcher and Emerson, 2009; Gomes and Espinosa, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Bell and Felsenfeld, 2000; Witcher and Emerson, 2009; Gomes and Espinosa, 2010.

claim: Regulation of the imprinted Igf2 and H19 genes pivots on parent of origin differences in the DNA methylation pattern and the activity of a CTCF-dependent boundary element upstream of the H19 gene.
source: For example, regulation of the imprinted Igf2 and H19 genes pivots on parent of origin differences in the DNA methylation pattern and consequently the activity of a CTCF-dependent boundary element upstream of the H19 gene (Bell and Felsenfeld, 2000; Hark et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Bell and Felsenfeld, 2000; Hark et al., 2000.

claim: The insulating activity of the Fab-7 boundary depends upon distinct, stage specific boundary factors.
source: In previous studies we discovered that the insulating activity of one of the Drosophila Bithorax (BX-C) complex boundaries, Fab-7, depends upon distinct, stage specific boundary factors (Schweinsberg and Schedl, 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Schweinsberg and Schedl, 2004.

claim: Fab-7 is required to ensure the functional autonomy of its flanking parasegment specific cis-regulatory domains, iab-6 and iab-7.
source: Like other boundaries in BX-C, Fab-7 is required to ensure the functional autonomy of its flanking parasegment specific cis-regulatory domains, iab-6 (parasegment 11) and iab-7 (parasegment 12) (Gyurkovics et al., 1990; Figure 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Gyurkovics et al., 1990 and reference to Figure 1.

claim: When Fab-7 is deleted, the iab-6 and iab-7 domains fuse into a single domain that incorrectly specifies parasegment 11.
source: When Fab-7 is deleted the iab-6 and iab-7 domains no longer function independently and instead fuse into a single domain that incorrectly specifies parasegment 11.
evidence: This statement describes the functional consequence of Fab-7 deletion based on prior studies.

claim: Fab-7 can block interactions between enhancers/silencers and promoters in the context of the endogenous BX-C.
source: While the primary function of Fab-7 in BX-C is to prevent inappropriate crosstalk between regulatory elements in iab-6 and iab-7, it can also block interactions between enhancers/silencers and promoters both in the context of the endogenous BX-C (Mihaly et al., 1997) and in reporter gene assays (Hagstrom et al., 1996; see Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Mihaly et al., 1997.

claim: Fab-7 can block interactions between enhancers/silencers and promoters in reporter gene assays.
source: While the primary function of Fab-7 in BX-C is to prevent inappropriate crosstalk between regulatory elements in iab-6 and iab-7, it can also block interactions between enhancers/silencers and promoters both in the context of the endogenous BX-C (Mihaly et al., 1997) and in reporter gene assays (Hagstrom et al., 1996; see Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Hagstrom et al., 1996 and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Fab-7 boundary spans a DNA segment of 1.2 kb that contains two major nuclease hypersensitive sites, HS1 and HS2, and a minor hypersensitive site.
source: Transgene assays and deletion mutations within BX-C have shown that the Fab-7 boundary spans a DNA segment of 1.2 kb that contains two major nuclease hypersensitive sites, HS1 and HS2, and a minor hypersensitive site '*' (see Figure 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by prior transgene and deletion studies and is illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Fab-7 has insulating activity throughout development apparently irrespective of tissue or cell type both in the context of BX-C and in transgene assays.
source: Like other well-characterized Drosophila boundaries, it has insulating activity throughout development apparently irrespective of tissue or cell type both in the context of BX-C and in transgene assays.
evidence: This statement is based on prior characterization studies of Fab-7.

claim: The constitutive boundary function of Fab-7 is generated by sub-elements whose activity is developmentally restricted.
source: However, Fab-7 appears unusual in that its constitutive boundary function is generated by sub-elements whose activity is developmentally restricted.
evidence: This statement is supported by the studies described in the manuscript, particularly those by Schweinsberg and Schedl, 2004.

claim: Mutations in the proximal pair of GAGA sites weaken Fab-7 boundary activity in early embryos but have little effect from mid-embryogenesis onwards.
source: Mutations in the proximal pair weaken boundary activity in early embryos, but have little effect from mid-embryogenesis onwards.
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Schweinsberg et al., 2004.

claim: Mutations in the central pair of GAGA sites weaken Fab-7 boundary activity during mid-embryogenesis and in adults, but not in early embryos.
source: In contrast, mutations in the central pair weaken boundary activity during mid-embryogenesis and in adults, but not in early embryos.
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Schweinsberg et al., 2004.

claim: Multimers of small fragments from the distal half of HS1 block enhancer-promoter interactions from mid-embryogenesis onwards.
source: Multimers of small 2- to 400-bp fragments from the distal half of HS1 were found to block enhancer-promoter interactions from mid-embryogenesis onwards even more efficiently that the intact Fab-7 boundary.
evidence: This statement describes experimental findings from prior studies.

claim: A multimerized 236-bp fragment pHS1 containing the proximal pair of GAGA sites has enhancer blocking activity during early embryogenesis, but not thereafter.
source: Conversely, a multimerized 236-bp fragment, pHS1, containing the proximal pair of GAGA sites has enhancer blocking activity during early embryogenesis, but not thereafter.
evidence: This statement describes experimental findings illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Two partial Fab-7 deletions in BX-C that remove the distal half of HS1 plus H2 but retain the proximal pHS1 sequence function as boundaries during early embryogenesis but not later in development.
source: Consistent with these transgene results, two partial Fab-7 deletions in BX-C that remove the distal half of HS1 plus H2, but retain the proximal pHS1 sequence including pair of GAGA sites function as boundaries during early embryogenesis but not later in development (Schweinsberg and Schedl, 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Schweinsberg and Schedl, 2004.

claim: The early boundary activity of partial Fab-7 deletions depends upon the GAGA factor.
source: In addition, the early boundary activity of these partial deletions depends upon the GAGA factor (Schweinsberg et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Schweinsberg et al., 2004.

claim: Elba DNA binding activity is present in extracts from early 0–6 hr embryos.
source: It is present in extracts from early 0–6 hr embryos, a period when pHS1 boundary activity is high.
evidence: This statement is supported by EMSA experiments described in the manuscript and in Aoki et al., 2008.

claim: Elba DNA binding activity is largely absent in extracts from older 6–12 hr embryos.
source: In contrast, in extracts from older 6–12 hr embryos, where pHS1 boundary activity in vivo is largely absent, only little Elba is detected.
evidence: This statement is supported by EMSA experiments described in the manuscript and in Aoki et al., 2008.

claim: Elba recognizes an asymmetric 8-bp sequence, CCAATAAG.
source: Elba recognizes an asymmetric 8-bp sequence, CCAATAAG (see Figure 1D), which is conserved in the Fab-7 elements of other Drosophila species including the distant melanogaster relative D. virilis.
evidence: This statement is supported by EMSA experiments and sequence analysis described in Aoki et al., 2008.

claim: The Elba recognition sequence is conserved in the Fab-7 elements of other Drosophila species including D. virilis.
source: Elba recognizes an asymmetric 8-bp sequence, CCAATAAG (see Figure 1D), which is conserved in the Fab-7 elements of other Drosophila species including the distant melanogaster relative D. virilis.
evidence: This statement is based on sequence conservation analysis.

claim: Mutations in the Elba recognition sequence that disrupt Elba binding in nuclear extracts compromise pHS1 insulator activity in vivo.
source: We found that mutations in the recognition sequence that disrupt Elba binding in nuclear extracts compromise pHS1 insulator activity in vivo.
evidence: This statement is supported by data from Aoki et al., 2008 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Multimerizing the Elba recognition sequence is sufficient to confer early insulating activity.
source: Conversely, multimerizing the Elba recognition sequence is sufficient to confer early insulating activity (Aoki et al., 2008; see Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by data from Aoki et al., 2008 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Elba boundary factor is an unusual hetero-tripartite protein complex consisting of Elba1, Elba2, and Elba3.
source: Using this purification strategy, we show that the Elba boundary factor is an unusual hetero-tripartite protein complex.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry and in vitro reconstitution experiments.

claim: Elba1 and Elba2 share a conserved C-terminal 'BEN domain'.
source: Two of the proteins, Elba1 and Elba2, share a conserved C-terminal 'BEN domain' (Abhiman et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by sequence analysis and citation to Abhiman et al., 2008.

claim: Elba3 has no obvious conserved protein domains.
source: The third protein, Elba3, has no obvious conserved protein domains, but is encoded by a gene that is closely linked to Elba1.
evidence: This statement is based on sequence analysis of Elba3.

claim: Elba3 is encoded by a gene that is closely linked to Elba1.
source: The third protein, Elba3, has no obvious conserved protein domains, but is encoded by a gene that is closely linked to Elba1.
evidence: This statement is based on genomic location analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: All three Elba proteins are required to reconstitute DNA binding activity in vitro.
source: All three Elba proteins are required to reconstitute DNA binding activity in vitro.
evidence: This statement is supported by in vitro translation and EMSA experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: DNA binding by the Elba complex depends upon the BEN domains in Elba1 and Elba2.
source: DNA binding depends upon the BEN domains in Elba1 and Elba2, while Elba3 mediates the assembly of an active Elba complex by interacting with the N-terminal domains of Elba1 and Elba2.
evidence: This statement is supported by deletion mutant experiments shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Elba3 mediates the assembly of an active Elba complex by interacting with the N-terminal domains of Elba1 and Elba2.
source: DNA binding depends upon the BEN domains in Elba1 and Elba2, while Elba3 mediates the assembly of an active Elba complex by interacting with the N-terminal domains of Elba1 and Elba2.
evidence: This statement is supported by experiments shown in Figures 5 and 6 demonstrating that GST can substitute for Elba3 and that Elba3 is not required when GST-fused Elba1C and Elba2C are used.

claim: All three Elba proteins are present in the Elba complex detected in 0–6 hr nuclear extracts.
source: All three Elba proteins are present in the Elba complex detected in 0–6 hr nuclear extracts and all three are required for chromatin domain boundary function in vivo.
evidence: This statement is supported by antibody supershift experiments shown in Figure 4D.

claim: All three Elba proteins are required for chromatin domain boundary function in vivo.
source: All three Elba proteins are present in the Elba complex detected in 0–6 hr nuclear extracts and all three are required for chromatin domain boundary function in vivo.
evidence: This statement is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 9.

claim: elba1 and elba3 are 'mid-blastula transition' genes.
source: Finally, because elba1 and elba3 are 'mid-blastula transition' genes, Elba only binds to its' target sequences in Fab-7 and confers insulator activity during early embryogenesis.
evidence: This statement is supported by Northern blot analysis shown in Figure 7 and citation to Singer and Lengyel, 1997.

claim: Elba only binds to its target sequences in Fab-7 during early embryogenesis.
source: Finally, because elba1 and elba3 are 'mid-blastula transition' genes, Elba only binds to its' target sequences in Fab-7 and confers insulator activity during early embryogenesis.
evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP experiments shown in Figure 8.

claim: Elba confers insulator activity only during early embryogenesis.
source: Finally, because elba1 and elba3 are 'mid-blastula transition' genes, Elba only binds to its' target sequences in Fab-7 and confers insulator activity during early embryogenesis.
evidence: This statement is supported by transgene assays and RNAi experiments shown in Figures 1 and 9.

claim: Three proteins were substantially enriched in the MSW1 fraction compared to all others in the cross-affinity purification.
source: Second, while there were still 176 unique proteins in the MSW1 fraction, three of these were substantially enriched compared to all others (Table 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Table 1.

claim: The three enriched proteins each had 16 or more confirmed peptides with high spectral counts and their sequence coverage was over 25%.
source: Each had 16 or more confirmed peptides with high spectral counts and their sequence coverage was over 25%.
evidence: This statement is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Table 1.

claim: Elba1 (CG12205) is encoded by a previously described mid-blastula transition gene, Bsg25A.
source: One protein, Elba1: CG12205, is encoded by a previously described mid-blastula transition gene, Bsg25A, of unknown function (Singer and Lengyel, 1997) while the other two, Elba2: CG9883 and Elba3: CG15634, are products of uncharacterized genes.
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Singer and Lengyel, 1997.

claim: Elba2 (CG9883) and Elba3 (CG15634) are products of uncharacterized genes.
source: One protein, Elba1: CG12205, is encoded by a previously described mid-blastula transition gene, Bsg25A, of unknown function (Singer and Lengyel, 1997) while the other two, Elba2: CG9883 and Elba3: CG15634, are products of uncharacterized genes.
evidence: This statement indicates that these genes had not been functionally characterized prior to this study.

claim: All three Elba proteins are approximately 40 kDa.
source: Although the three proteins have no previously known DNA binding domains, there are several intriguing connections. First, all three are ∼40 kDa, which is close in size to the protein species in nuclear extracts that is UV cross-linked to probes containing the Elba sequence (Aoki et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is based on the predicted molecular weights shown in Table 1 and comparison to UV cross-linking data.

claim: The C-terminal approximately 130 amino acids of Elba1 and Elba2 show extensive sequence similarities.
source: Second, the C-terminal ∼130 amino acids of Elba1 and Elba2 show extensive sequence similarities (Figure 3C).
evidence: This statement is supported by sequence alignment shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The BEN domain has been implicated in protein:protein interactions and transcriptional regulation.
source: Moreover, included within this region of similarity is a conserved ∼90 amino acids BEN domain (Figure 3B) that has been implicated in protein:protein interactions and transcriptional regulation (Cha et al., 1997; Mackler et al., 2000; Wang et al., 2006; Korutla et al., 2009; Duan et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Cha et al., 1997; Mackler et al., 2000; Wang et al., 2006; Korutla et al., 2009; Duan et al., 2011.

claim: Insensitive (Insv) functions in neurogenesis and Notch signaling.
source: One is a predicted isoform of the Mod(mdg4)C boundary factor, while the other is Insensitive (Insv) (Figure 3C), which functions in neurogenesis and Notch signaling (Duan et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Duan et al., 2011.

claim: The elba2 and Insv transcription units are paired with each other.
source: Interestingly, the elba2 and Insv transcription units are paired with each other (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by genomic location data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Elba3 transcription unit is located next to elba1.
source: Finally, though Elba3 differs from Elba1 and Elba2 in that it has no distinctive domains, its transcription unit is located next to elba1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1) just like the elba2 and insv pair.
evidence: This statement is supported by genomic location data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Within the BEN domain sequences, the closest human ortholog of Elba1 is BEND7.
source: Within the BEN domain sequences, the closest human ortholog of Elba1 is BEND7 (BEN domain-containing 7)/C10orf30 (29% identical, 46% positive), whereas for Elba2 the closest ortholog is BEND6/C6orf65 (29% identical, 53% positive).
evidence: This statement is supported by sequence alignment shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The closest human ortholog of Elba2 is BEND6.
source: Within the BEN domain sequences, the closest human ortholog of Elba1 is BEND7 (BEN domain-containing 7)/C10orf30 (29% identical, 46% positive), whereas for Elba2 the closest ortholog is BEND6/C6orf65 (29% identical, 53% positive).
evidence: This statement is supported by sequence alignment shown in Figure 3D.

claim: None of the individual Elba proteins shifted the Elba probe when translated alone.
source: Figure 4A shows that none shifted the Elba probe.
evidence: This statement is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Translating all three Elba mRNAs together generates a prominent shift that co-migrates with the Elba shift produced by 0–6 hr nuclear extracts.
source: We next translated all three mRNAs together. Strikingly, this combination generated a prominent shift that co-migrates with the Elba shift produced by 0–6 hr nuclear extracts (Figure 4A).
evidence: This statement is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: None of the pairwise combinations of Elba proteins had DNA binding activity.
source: Figure 4B shows that none of the pairwise combinations had DNA binding activity; however, it was possible to reconstitute the Elba shift by combining all three translation products.
evidence: This statement is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The sequence specificity of reconstituted Elba is the same as nuclear extract Elba.
source: Figure 4C shows that sequence specificity of reconstituted Elba is the same as nuclear extract Elba.
evidence: This statement is supported by competition EMSA data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: All six immune sera against Elba proteins give an Elba supershift in nuclear extracts.
source: Figure 4D shows that all six immune sera give an Elba supershift, while the Elba shift is unchanged by the corresponding pre-immune sera.
evidence: This statement is supported by antibody supershift data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The Elba factor in 0–6 hr nuclear extracts contains all three Elba proteins.
source: These findings indicate that the Elba factor in 0–6 hr nuclear extracts must also contain all three Elba proteins.
evidence: This statement is inferred from the antibody supershift experiments shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Weak DNA binding activity was detected when bacterially expressed N-terminal GST fusions of Elba1 and Elba2 were mixed in the absence of Elba3.
source: In preliminary experiments, we found very weak, but detectable DNA binding activity when we mixed bacterially expressed N-terminal GST (Glutahione-S-transferase) fusions of the two BEN domain proteins, Elba1 and Elba2, in the absence of Elba3.
evidence: This statement describes preliminary experimental observations.

claim: GST moieties might substitute for Elba3 by promoting the formation of GST-Elba1:GST-Elba2 heterodimers.
source: Since GST is known to form stable dimers, we reasoned that the GST moieties might be substituting for Elba3 by promoting the formation of GST-Elba1:GST-Elba2 heterodimers (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the known dimerization properties of GST and the experimental observation of weak DNA binding.

claim: The BEN domains in Elba1 and Elba2 are responsible for DNA recognition.
source: This finding together with the asymmetric Elba binding motif, CCAATAAG, suggested a model in which the BEN domains in Elba1 and Elba2 are responsible for DNA recognition, while the function of Elba3 is to bring Elba1 and Elba2 together so that they can form the DNA binding pocket (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a model proposed based on experimental observations and supported by deletion mutant experiments in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: The function of Elba3 is to bring Elba1 and Elba2 together so that they can form the DNA binding pocket.
source: This finding together with the asymmetric Elba binding motif, CCAATAAG, suggested a model in which the BEN domains in Elba1 and Elba2 are responsible for DNA recognition, while the function of Elba3 is to bring Elba1 and Elba2 together so that they can form the DNA binding pocket (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a model proposed based on experimental observations and supported by experiments showing GST can substitute for Elba3.

claim: Deleting the BEN domain from either Elba1 or Elba2 eliminates DNA binding activity.
source: Figure 5B shows that mixing the three full-length proteins (which have N-terminal FLAG tags as do all of the other proteins in Figure 5A) generates the Elba shift, while the shift is eliminated whenever a BEN domain deletion is used instead for reconstitution.
evidence: This statement is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Co-translation of GST-Elba1F and GST-Elba2F generates a prominent shift.
source: As shown in lane 6 of Figure 6A, a prominent shift is generated when these two GST fusions are co-translated.
evidence: This statement is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Individual GST-Elba1F and GST-Elba2F fusions fail to shift the Elba probe on their own.
source: In contrast, the individual GST fusions fail to shift the Elba probe on their own even though they are expected to form homodimers (Figure 6A, lanes 7 and 8).
evidence: This statement is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The GST-Elba1F:GST-Elba2F heterodimer can still form a trimeric complex with Elba3.
source: While GST can substitute for Elba3, the supershift generated by the addition of Elba3 (Figure 6A, lane 5) indicates that the GST-Elba1F:GST-Elba2F heterodimer is still able to form a trimeric complex with Elba3.
evidence: This statement is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: GST-Elba1C:GST-Elba2C heterodimer exhibits DNA binding activity with similar sequence specificity to the native hetero-tripartite Elba complex.
source: In addition to having roughly equivalent activity to the 'native' hetero-tripartite Elba complex generated by the three full length Elba proteins, the GST-Elba1C:GST-Elba2C heterodimer exhibits a similar sequence specificity (Figures 4C and 6C).
evidence: This statement is supported by competition EMSA data shown in Figures 4C and 6C.

claim: The addition of Elba3 to the two ElbaC proteins (without GST) does not reconstitute full DNA binding activity.
source: On the other hand, the two ElbaC proteins differ from the full length Elba1 and Elba2 proteins in two respects. Most importantly, the addition of Elba3 to the two ElbaC proteins (without the GST moiety) does not reconstitute full DNA binding activity (Figure 6D, lane 7).
evidence: This statement is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Elba3 orchestrates the formation of the hetero-tripartite complex by interacting with sequences in the N-terminal domains of Elba1 and Elba2.
source: This finding suggests that Elba3 orchestrates the formation of the hetero-tripartite complex by interacting with sequences in the N-terminal domains of Elba1 and Elba2 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Elba3 cannot reconstitute activity with ElbaC proteins lacking N-terminal domains.

claim: The shift generated by the GST-Elba1C:GST-Elba2C heterodimer is not supershifted by the addition of Elba3.
source: Consistent with this idea, the shift generated by the active GST-Elba1C:GST-Elba2C heterodimer differs from the full-length heterodimer in that it is not supershifted by the addition of Elba3 (Figure 6A, lane 12).
evidence: This statement is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The mixture of Elba1C and Elba2C proteins (lacking GST) gives a faint shift that can be detected in long exposures.
source: A second potentially interesting difference is that the mixture of Elba1C and Elba2C proteins (lacking GST) gives a faint shift that can be detected in long (Figure 6D, lane 8 filled arrowhead) but not short (Figure 6A, lane 16) exposures.
evidence: This statement is supported by EMSA data shown in Figures 6A and 6D.

claim: There are weakly active hetero-dimerization motifs in the C-terminal halves of Elba1 and Elba2.
source: Although further studies will be required, it would appear that there are weakly active hetero-dimerization motifs in the C-terminal halves of Elba1 and Elba2 that become more readily accessible when the N-terminus of the two proteins is removed.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the weak DNA binding activity observed with Elba1C and Elba2C proteins.

claim: Neither elba1 nor elba3 is expressed during oogenesis.
source: Figure 7 and Figure 7—figure supplement 1 show that neither is expressed during oogenesis, and that their mRNAs are largely absent in 0–2 hr embryos.
evidence: This statement is supported by Northern blot data shown in Figure 7 and modEncode data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: elba1 and elba3 mRNAs are largely absent in 0–2 hr embryos.
source: Figure 7 and Figure 7—figure supplement 1 show that neither is expressed during oogenesis, and that their mRNAs are largely absent in 0–2 hr embryos.
evidence: This statement is supported by Northern blot data shown in Figure 7 and modEncode data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expression of elba1 and elba3 peaks at the blastoderm stage (2–4 hr).
source: Consistent with the previous identification of elba1 as a mid-blastula transition gene (Singer and Lengyel, 1997), expression of elba1 and also elba3 peaks at the blastoderm stage (2–4 hr), and then disappears.
evidence: This statement is supported by Northern blot data shown in Figure 7 and citation to Singer and Lengyel, 1997.

claim: The disappearance of elba1 and elba3 mRNAs occurs in the same time frame as the loss of boundary activity in transgene embryos and DNA binding activity in nuclear extracts.
source: The disappearance of the elba1 and elba3 mRNAs occurs in the same time frame as the loss of boundary activity in transgene embryos and DNA binding activity in nuclear extracts.
evidence: This statement correlates the temporal expression patterns with functional data from earlier experiments.

claim: elba2 and insv appear to be expressed throughout much of embryogenesis.
source: While expression of elba1 and elba3 is developmentally restricted, elba2 and its neighboring ortholog, insv, appear to be expressed throughout much embryogenesis.
evidence: This statement is supported by Northern blot data shown in Figure 7.

claim: elba2 and insv are expressed during oogenesis and likely are maternally deposited.
source: Moreover, both are expressed during oogenesis and likely are maternally deposited, as high levels are present in 0–2 hr embryo before zygotic transcription is activated.
evidence: This statement is supported by Northern blot data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Elba1 and Elba2 are bound to the Fab-7 Elba sequence in 2–5 hr embryos.
source: Figure 8A,B shows that as predicted Elba1 and Elba2 are bound to the Fab-7 Elba sequence in 2–5 hr embryos, but not to control sequences from the twine (twe) and Sex-lethal (Sxl) genes.
evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 8A,B.

claim: Elba1 and Elba2 are not bound to control sequences from the twine and Sex-lethal genes in 2–5 hr embryos.
source: Figure 8A,B shows that as predicted Elba1 and Elba2 are bound to the Fab-7 Elba sequence in 2–5 hr embryos, but not to control sequences from the twine (twe) and Sex-lethal (Sxl) genes.
evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 8A,B.

claim: Neither Elba1 nor Elba2 appears to be bound to Fab-7 in 9–12 hr embryos.
source: In contrast, neither protein appears to be bound to Fab-7 in 9–12 hr embryos.
evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 8A,B.

claim: Injection of dsRNA specific for elba1 disrupts UPS blocking activity of pHS1×4.
source: In contrast, UPS blocking activity was disrupted when embryos were injected with dsRNA specific for one of the Elba proteins. For both elba1 and elba3, most fell into Class 3–5, while for elba2 most were Class 2–4.
evidence: This statement is supported by RNAi injection data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Injection of dsRNA specific for elba2 disrupts UPS blocking activity of pHS1×4.
source: In contrast, UPS blocking activity was disrupted when embryos were injected with dsRNA specific for one of the Elba proteins. For both elba1 and elba3, most fell into Class 3–5, while for elba2 most were Class 2–4.
evidence: This statement is supported by RNAi injection data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Injection of dsRNA specific for elba3 disrupts UPS blocking activity of pHS1×4.
source: In contrast, UPS blocking activity was disrupted when embryos were injected with dsRNA specific for one of the Elba proteins. For both elba1 and elba3, most fell into Class 3–5, while for elba2 most were Class 2–4.
evidence: This statement is supported by RNAi injection data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Injection of dsRNA for insv did not disrupt boundary activity of pHS1×4.
source: The loss of boundary activity is specific to constituents of the Elba complex, as injection of dsRNA for the closely related insv did not disrupt boundary activity.
evidence: This statement is supported by RNAi injection data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: The disruption of boundary activity in RNAi experiments was greatest for elba1 and elba3.
source: Similar results were obtained in two other sets of pHS1×4 dsRNA injection experiments, and in experiments using embryos transgenic for the Elba multimer (Figure 9—figure supplement 1). Like the set shown here, the disruption of boundary activity in these experiments was greatest for elba1 and elba3, while smaller effects were observed for elba2.
evidence: This statement is supported by RNAi injection data shown in Figure 9 and Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: The differences in sensitivity to dsRNA between elba genes are likely due to differences in expression pattern of the elba mRNAs.
source: The differences in expression pattern of the elba mRNAs most likely accounts for this differences in sensitivity to dsRNA.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the RNAi results based on the expression data showing maternal deposition of elba2 but not elba1 or elba3.

claim: There is a substantial pool of maternally derived elba2 mRNAs that could already be translationally engaged at the time of dsRNA injection.
source: While expression of elba1 and elba3 would be turned on in most instances after injection of the dsRNA, there is a substantial pool of maternally derived elba2 mRNAs that could already be translationally engaged at the time of injection.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the Northern blot data showing maternal elba2 expression.

claim: A constitutive insulator like Fab-7 may utilize developmentally limited factors like Elba to optimize combinations with other nearby BX-C boundaries or the Abdominal-B promoter.
source: Thus, the use of stage specific factors at Fab-7 could reflect a need to optimize combinations with other nearby BX-C boundaries or the Abdominal-B promoter (Kyrchanova et al., 2008b, 2011).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for why Fab-7 uses stage-specific factors, supported by citations to Kyrchanova et al., 2008b, 2011.

claim: When heterologous boundaries are used to replace Fab-7 in BX-C, they are unable to provide bypass activity.
source: When heterologous boundaries are used to replace Fab-7 in BX-C, they are unable to provide bypass activity, while their insulating activity can be lost in a stage and tissue specific fashion (Hogga et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Hogga et al., 2001.

claim: Fab-7 is able to replace Fab-8.
source: In contrast, Fab-7 is able to replace Fab-8 (Iampietro et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Iampietro et al., 2008.

claim: The boundary activity of Fab-7 in a foreign environment is context dependent and varies during development.
source: Likewise, the boundary activity of Fab-7 in a foreign environment is not only context dependent, but also varies during development (Gohl et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Gohl et al., 2011.

claim: Bypass is observed when Fab-7 is combined with the neighboring boundaries Fab-6 and Fab-8.
source: They found that bypass is observed when Fab-7 is combined with the neighboring boundaries Fab-6 and Fab-8, while bypass interactions with boundaries from elsewhere in BX-C are only weak at best.
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Kyrchanova et al., 2011.

claim: Boundary bypass is mediated by homologous protein:protein interactions.
source: Interestingly, in the cases that have been analyzed most thoroughly, boundary bypass is mediated by homologous protein:protein interactions (Kyrchanova et al., 2008a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Kyrchanova et al., 2008a.

claim: Bypass is observed when multimerized binding sites for the dCTCF boundary factor are paired, but not when dCTCF binding sites are paired with sites for Zw5.
source: Thus, bypass is observed when multimerized binding sites for the dCTCF boundary factor are paired, but not when dCTCF binding sites are paired with sites for example Zw5.
evidence: This statement describes experimental findings about boundary bypass specificity.

claim: Fab-8 utilizes dCTCF.
source: Though Fab-8 differs from Fab-7 in that it utilizes dCTCF (Holohan et al., 2007; Kyrchanova et al., 2011), EMSA experiments with 0–6 hr and 6–12 hr nuclear extracts indicate that they also have binding sites for several of the same stage specific factors (Aoki et al., 2008; Wolle et al., unpublished data).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Holohan et al., 2007; Kyrchanova et al., 2011.

claim: EMSA experiments indicate that Fab-7 and Fab-8 have binding sites for several of the same stage specific factors including Elba.
source: Though Fab-8 differs from Fab-7 in that it utilizes dCTCF (Holohan et al., 2007; Kyrchanova et al., 2011), EMSA experiments with 0–6 hr and 6–12 hr nuclear extracts indicate that they also have binding sites for several of the same stage specific factors (Aoki et al., 2008; Wolle et al., unpublished data). These include sites for the Elba factor, and sites for two different late (6–12 hr) stage specific factors.
evidence: This statement is supported by EMSA data from Aoki et al., 2008 and unpublished data.

claim: Elba2 could function as an insulator in other contexts using different protein partners after Elba1 and Elba3 disappear.
source: While Elba2 can't bind to the Elba sequence on its own, it could function as an insulator in other contexts using different protein partners and presumably also recognition sequences.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis about the potential function of Elba2 in later development.

claim: Insv is a plausible partner for Elba2 after Elba1 and Elba3 disappear.
source: A plausible partner would be the Notch signaling pathway protein Insv, which is encoded by a tightly linked gene that has a similar expression pattern to elba2.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis based on the genomic linkage and expression patterns of elba2 and insv.

claim: Insv and its closest mammalian relatives, the NAC proteins, are believed to regulate transcription by acting as co-repressors.
source: Insv and its closest mammalian relatives, the NAC proteins (which are thought to function as stem cell pluripotency genes, as well as in cocaine addiction and cancer), are believed to regulate transcription by acting as co-repressors (Cha et al., 1997; Mackler et al., 2000; Wang et al., 2006; Korutla et al., 2009; Duan et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Cha et al., 1997; Mackler et al., 2000; Wang et al., 2006; Korutla et al., 2009; Duan et al., 2011.

claim: The BEN domains of Elba1 and Elba2 are essential for DNA binding, suggesting that Insv and mammalian counterparts may be sequence specific DNA binding proteins rather than co-repressors.
source: However, since our findings indicate that the BEN domains of Elba1 and Elba2 are essential for DNA binding, it would be reasonable to suppose that Insv as well as the mammalian counterparts are not co-repressors, but are rather sequence specific DNA binding proteins.
evidence: This is a speculative reinterpretation of the function of Insv and NAC proteins based on the findings about Elba BEN domains.

claim: CTCF was initially thought to be a transcriptional repressor.
source: Interestingly, like members of the BEN domain protein family, CTCF was initially thought to be a transcriptional repressor (Filippova et al., 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Filippova et al., 1996.

claim: Other members of the BEN family besides the two Elba proteins may function as insulators restricting the action of nearby enhancer elements instead of directly repressing transcription.
source: Thus, a seemingly plausible speculation would be that other members of the BEN family besides the two Elba proteins function as insulators restricting the action of nearby enhancer elements instead of directly repressing transcription.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis based on the findings about Elba and the analogy to CTCF.

claim: One of the mammalian BEN domain proteins, SMAR1, is a component of the nuclear matrix and associates with Matrix Attachment Regions.
source: Potentially supporting this idea is the finding that one of the mammalian BEN domain proteins, SMAR1, is a component of the nuclear matrix and associates with Matrix Attachment Regions (MARS) (Chattopadhyay et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Chattopadhyay et al., 2000.

claim: If other BEN domain proteins function as insulators, CTCF would not be the only vertebrate insulator protein.
source: If this were the case, this would mean that CTCF is not the only vertebrate insulator protein.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the speculation that other BEN domain proteins may function as insulators.

claim: Modulating the expression or activity of Elba2, Insv or NAC1 in different tissues or cell types could change the regulatory domain landscapes and potentially alter global patterns of gene expression.
source: Also as is case for the Elba complex, modulating the expression or activity of Elba2, Insv or NAC1 in different tissues or cell types could change the regulatory domain landscapes, and potentially alter global patterns of gene expression.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis about the potential regulatory role of these proteins in defining chromatin domains.
